articles.title: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
articles.summary: Despite having the highest voter turnout in nearly three decades, Israel's elections have had no clear winner. What does this mean for the country, asks the BBC's Yolande Knell.
articles.body:
A dramatic deadlock had been widely forecast as Israelis surged to the polls – with turnout reaching more than 77%.

Despite the historic number of voters, no clear winner has emerged. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for a "strong" right-wing government and his Likud is set to be the biggest party in the Knesset, Israel's parliament

However, Netanyahu's main rival, the former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, has insisted Israel voted to end Netanyahu's term.

But with neither party securing a clear majority, what does this mean for the future of Israel?

The BBC's Yolande Knell reports from Jerusalem.

articles.title: Reporter caught in violent Paris protests recalls how 'all of a sudden, it exploded' after peaceful march
articles.summary: A New York Post reporter describes how masked newcomers turned a peaceful Paris march of 100,000 into violent chaos as fury rages against the government.
articles.body:
A New York Post reporter caught in the chaos of violent protests in Paris recounted how a peaceful march of more than 100,000 people took a frightening turn.

"All of a sudden, it exploded," Gabrielle Fahmy recalled Tuesday on "Fox & Friends."

"When it got dark, when they reached the endpoint of the march, it's like they didn't know what to do anymore," she continued.

"Tensions had been mounting. These new people I saw sort of joined the protest towards the end. We saw some people arrive by metro. They were dressed differently, hiding their faces. They had masks, and that's sort of when I could see things start to shift."

Fahmy told co-host Brian Kilmeade the protests were peaceful for several hours, describing the transition from police leading the crowd to violence erupting in the streets as "very surreal."

She said the newcomers appeared to be younger demonstrators, many in their late teens and early 20s, and suggested some might have been "factions of the far-left."

The protests began as student-led demonstrations over teacher shortages and poor conditions at schools but have since evolved into a broader anti-government movement, with protesters voicing frustration over the cost of living and other grievances.

"The people there on Saturday, it was a general sort of cost of living that they were complaining about," Fahmy recalled.

"There's not enough jobs, they're not making enough money, they can't afford to put food on the table. But also anti-government, they are fed up with Emmanuel Macron , who's on his way out anyway. But, it was just a very general, general reason."

Fahmy also recalled seeing Palestinian flags, noting that "everybody with a grievance" seemed to have joined the demonstrations.

Separate protests have also turned violent in Rome and Albania's capital, Tirana, where demonstrators set government buildings on fire.

Fox News' James Cirrone and Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

articles.title: Isenção de IPVA para motoristas de app na Paraíba é aprovada | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto de autoria do governo estadual altera a lei do IPVA e prevê que critérios para concessão do benefício sejam definidos por decreto.
articles.summary: Aprovada pela ALPB, a isenção de IPVA para motoristas de aplicativo na Paraíba começa em 2027 e terá critérios definidos por decreto do governo estadual em novembro.
articles.body:
Motorista de aplicativo — Foto: Reprodução/Freepik

A Assembleia Legislativa da Paraíba (ALPB) aprovou, nesta quarta-feira (28), uma alteração na lei que regulamenta o Imposto sobre a Propriedade de Veículos Automotores ( IPVA ) no estado para incluir motoristas de aplicativo entre os beneficiários da isenção do tributo. A medida começa a valer em janeiro de 2027.

A proposta é de autoria do Poder Executivo e altera a Lei Estadual nº 11.007/2017. Os critérios para que os motoristas tenham direito ao benefício serão definidos em um decreto do governo estadual, previsto para ser publicado no fim de novembro.

O governador Lucas Ribeiro (PP) anunciou o envio da proposta à Assembleia Legislativa na terça-feira (27), em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais. A mudança inclui na legislação os veículos utilizados para o transporte de passageiros por meio de plataformas digitais.

De acordo com governo estadual, a medida considera a importância econômica e social do trabalho realizado pelos motoristas de aplicativo, além do papel da atividade como fonte de renda para os profissionais.

O texto aprovado estabelece que a isenção estará condicionada à manutenção dos serviços de transporte por aplicativo em território paraibano. As condições específicas para a concessão do benefício ainda dependem da regulamentação do governo.

articles.title: BTS em São Paulo: Procura por hotéis sobe 50% para shows no Morumbi | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo de k-pop coreano se apresenta no Estádio do Morumbi nesta quarta (28) e nos dias 30 e 31.
articles.summary: Shows do BTS em São Paulo fazem buscas por hotéis crescerem 50%, tornando a capital o único destino nacional com alta na procura durante as datas no Morumbi.
articles.body:
Grupo sul-coreano de K-pop BTS se apresenta em outubro no Brasil — Foto: Reprodução

Os três shows que o grupo de k-pop coreano BTS fará em São Paulo fizeram a procura por hospedagem na cidade crescer 50% no período.

Os dados são de um levantamento do site Hoteis.com, que registraram um crescimento intenso nas buscas para as datas dos shows, que começam nesta quarta-feira (28) no Estádio do Morumbi, e também irão ocorrer nos dias 30 e 31.

O aumento de 50% na procura, em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, foi para estadias entre 19 de outubro e 1º de novembro de 2026.

São Paulo foi o único destino nacional a registrar crescimento no período, enquanto cidades como Rio de Janeiro, Belo Horizonte e Recife sofreram queda nas buscas.

articles.title: Imagens aéreas mostram dimensão do acidente com trens na Espanha | G1
articles.standfirst: A causa do acidente e o número de feridos ainda estão sendo apurados. O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez, lamentou o acidente nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: A causa do acidente e o número de feridos ainda estão sendo apurados. O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez, lamentou o acidente nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Imagens aéreas mostram a destruição causada pela colisão entre dois trens de alta velocidade na Espanha nesta quarta (veja acima).

Segundo a porta-voz, um trem da Renfe e um trem da Iryo colidiram pouco depois das 9h do horário local - 5h de Brasília -, entre as cidades de Mora e Orgaz, causando o descarrilamento de dois vagões.

A causa do acidente e o número de feridos ainda estão sendo apurados, mas a porta-voz do governo local, da região de Castilla La Mancha, Ester Padilla, confirmou que ao menos 64 pessoas morreram e 80 ficaram feridas.

Ao todo, 147 pessoas estavam viajando no trem da Iryo e 397 no trem da Renfe.

Imagens aéreas mostram vagões descarrilados — Foto: Guarda Civil / Divulgação

Imagens da emissora regional Castilla La Mancha Television mostram um trem descarrilado com pelo menos um vagão ainda sobre um trecho elevado dos trilhos, enquanto metal retorcido, painéis quebrados e destroços podem ser vistos espalhados por um aterro abaixo da linha férrea.

Segundo uma fonte ouvida pela agência de notícias Reuters, o trem operado pela Iryo estava parado perto de Toledo por ordem da Adif, empresa gestora da infraestrutura ferroviária, devido a uma falha de sinalização, quando foi atingido pelo trem da Renfe.

As duas empresas ainda não responderam aos pedidos de comentários da Reuters. A circulação ferroviária está interrompida entre Madrid , Ciudad Real e Andalucía.

Equipes de resgate trabalham no local da colisão entre dois trens de alta velocidade, entre as cidades de Mora e Orgaz, perto de Toledo, na Espanha, em 28 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Violeta Santos Moura

Na rede social X, o primeiro-ministro, Pedro Sánchez , lamentou o acidente em um primeiro pronunciamento:

"Estou chocado com o grave acidente de trem em Toledo. Meu carinho, solidariedade e apoio a todas as vítimas e suas famílias".

A ministra da Saúde, Mónica García, fez um apelo em uma publicação no X para que as pessoas doassem sangue.

O Rei da Espanha , Felipe VI, falou sobre o acidente enquanto participava de um ato nas proximidades de Valência:

"A primeira coisa é lamentar essa tragédia terrível. Transmitir às famílias os nossos pêsames, a nossa tristeza, o nosso apoio, o nosso carinho em um momento tão duro, tão difícil".

A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, ao tomar conhecimento do acidente, afirmou que "hoje a Europa chora".

O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, classificou a tragédia como um "terrível drama ferroviário".

Manuel Galán, prefeito de Urda, cidade próxima a Toledo, na região central do país, disse que os serviços de emergência lhe pediram para preparar um ginásio poliesportivo para acomodar os feridos.

A agenda do dia do premiê, publicada no site do governo espanhol, foi cancelada. O Partido Popular, da oposição, também cancelou todos os eventos de campanha, segundo um porta-voz.

articles.title: Snapchat é julgado nos EUA pela 1ª vez por vício em redes sociais | G1
articles.standfirst: Júri vai analisar acusações de que as plataformas foram projetadas para gerar dependência e causar danos à saúde mental de crianças e adolescentes; Mark Zuckerberg e Evan Spiegel devem depor em novembro.
articles.summary: Júri vai analisar acusações de que as plataformas foram projetadas para gerar dependência e causar danos à saúde mental de crianças e adolescentes.
articles.body:
Snapchat é julgado nos EUA pela primeira vez — Foto: Richard Drew/AP Foto

A plataforma de mensagens Snapchat terá que se defender, pela primeira vez, diante de um júri contra acusações de vício em redes sociais entre os jovens , ao lado do Instagram ( Meta ), em um novo julgamento que começa nesta quarta-feira (28) em Los Angeles.

Nos últimos anos, foram apresentados milhares de processos em tribunais locais, estaduais e federais por todos os Estados Unidos, contendo diversas acusações sobre supostos danos a crianças e adolescentes causados por essas plataformas .

A seleção dos jurados começa nesta quarta-feira (28), e as audiências, que devem prosseguir até 4 de novembro, estão previstas para durar até meados de dezembro . A Snap, empresa matriz do Snapchat , e a Meta ainda podem optar por um acordo antes do veredicto.

Espera-se que os responsáveis pela Meta e pela Snap, Mark Zuckerberg e Evan Spiegel, prestem depoimento em meados de novembro, assim como o chefe do Instagram, Adam Mosseri, segundo os advogados das partes demandantes.

Elas acusam as plataformas de terem sido projetadas para gerar dependência , resultando em quadros de depressão, ansiedade, transtornos alimentares e automutilação.

articles.title: Rodoviária Velha de Taubaté: Prefeitura planeja concessão privada | G1
articles.standfirst: Processo de licitação deve começar após estudo de viabilidade econômica e financeira; prédio tem 80 boxes comerciais e recebe linhas de ônibus municipais e intermunicipais.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Taubaté inicia estudos para conceder a Rodoviária Velha à iniciativa privada, buscando solucionar problemas estruturais no terminal de 80 boxes.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Taubaté planeja conceder Rodoviária Velha à iniciativa privada — Foto: Reprodução/Street View

A Prefeitura de Taubaté informou, nesta quarta-feira (28), que planeja conceder a administração da Rodoviária Velha à iniciativa privada. Segundo o secretário de Serviços Públicos, José Sodário Viana, o processo de licitação deve começar após a conclusão de um estudo de viabilidade econômica e financeira. A expectativa é que o procedimento seja iniciado em breve.

O terminal é utilizado principalmente por passageiros das linhas de ônibus municipais e também por pessoas que viajam para cidades vizinhas. De acordo com a Prefeitura, a proposta é escolher uma empresa para assumir a gestão do espaço por meio de uma concessão.

Atualmente, a operação diária do terminal é gerida por uma associação de comerciantes. O prédio tem 80 boxes comerciais, dos quais 70 estão ocupados e 10 estão vazios.

A associação informou que concorda com a possibilidade de uma administração privada, desde que a mudança não resulte em aumento de taxas para os comerciantes. A preocupação é que custos mais altos dificultem a permanência dos estabelecimentos no local.

A Rodoviária Velha também recebe reclamações sobre as condições estruturais. Entre os problemas observados estão falhas nos banheiros públicos, como a falta de alguns mictórios no banheiro masculino.

O terminal é um espaço de grande circulação de passageiros, que utilizam o local para embarque e desembarque em linhas municipais e intermunicipais.

Outros espaços públicos na mira de concessões

A Rodoviária Velha é mais um espaço público que a Prefeitura de Taubaté pretende conceder à iniciativa privada.

Na semana passada, o município anunciou a intenção de conceder a administração do Teatro Metrópole e dos serviços de iluminação pública.

Em processos anteriores, a Prefeitura também obteve autorização para conceder sete parques municipais, entre eles o Parque do Itaim e o Parque Jardim das Nações. No entanto, os processos de licitação para esses espaços ainda não foram abertos.

articles.title: Merenda Chef: concurso define novas receitas da rede Faetec | G1
articles.standfirst: Final do concurso reúne 10 profissionais; 60 se inscreveram na competição, que busca criar novos pratos e valorizar quem trabalha nas cozinhas da rede de ensino.
articles.summary: O concurso Merenda Chef reuniu finalistas que criaram pratos para renovar o cardápio escolar da Faetec e valorizar o trabalho dos profissionais das cozinhas da rede.
articles.body:
Omelete com legumes, carne moída à parmegiana e até um "exibidinho" de carne. Receitas preparadas diariamente nas cozinhas da Faetec ganharam um ingrediente a mais nesta quarta-feira (28): a disputa para conquistar os jurados do concurso “Merenda Chef” .

A receita vencedora entrará no cardápio oficial das unidades da Faetec. O 1º colocado receberá R$ 1 mil , enquanto o 2º ganhará R$ 500 e o 3º levará R$ 300 .

Ao todo, 60 merendeiros se inscreveram na competição e 10 chegaram à final . Eles tiveram que preparar e apresentar suas receitas a uma banca formada por professoras de gastronomia, nutricionistas, um profissional da área de informática e dois estudantes do ensino superior de informática.

Além do sabor, os concorrentes capricharam na apresentação e explicaram as escolhas feitas para tornar os pratos mais atraentes para os estudantes.

Omelete acompanhada de salada foi uma das apostas do concurso — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A merendeira Fernanda dos Santos Coutinho apostou em uma omelete acompanhada de salada . Segundo ela, a ideia foi encontrar uma maneira de aumentar a aceitação dos legumes pelas crianças.

“Muitas vezes, as crianças não aceitam legumes. Então preparei a omelete, fiz os ovos com legumes e a salada para eles poderem aceitar mais”, contou.

A estratégia agradou à banca. A professora de gastronomia Lucilia da Silva Barreto elogiou a textura, a temperatura e o tempero da omelete. Já a também professora Michele Andrade destacou que os legumes ficam praticamente "escondidos" no preparo.

Depois da avaliação, Fernanda não escondeu a emoção. Para ela, chegar à final representa “uma valorização” e “um reconhecimento” do trabalho realizado nas cozinhas da rede.

Outro finalista, André Luiz, que trabalha como merendeiro há 28 anos, apresentou uma carne moída à parmegiana . A receita também arrancou elogios. Um dos jurados destacou o uso do coentro e a combinação da carne com a muçarela.

Carne moída à parmegiana foi outra aposta no concurso — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A nutricionista Pilar Matarate explicou que o objetivo do projeto é também renovar as opções oferecidas aos estudantes.

“A ideia do projeto é promover a inclusão de novas receitas que os alunos possam degustar, mudar o cardápio e valorizar os profissionais que atuam nas cozinhas da rede Faetec”, afirmou.

A disputa ainda contou com a auxiliar de cozinha Tamires dos Santos, que apresentou aos jurados um “exibidinho de carne”.

O resultado não foi divulgado durante a final . Segundo a organização, as receitas apresentadas serão analisadas para a definição do primeiro, segundo e terceiro lugares.

articles.title: Acidente entre trens na Espanha foi causado por falha no sistema de controle, diz governo | G1
articles.standfirst: Pelo menos 64 pessoas morreram na colisão entre dois trens de alta velocidade, perto de Toledo.
articles.summary: Pelo menos 64 pessoas morreram na colisão entre dois trens de alta velocidade, perto de Toledo.
articles.body:
O acidente entre dois trens de alta velocidade que colidiram na Espanha , causando ao menos 64 mortes nesta quarta-feira (28), foi causado por uma falha no sistema de controle, segundo o governo espanhol.

Em coletiva de imprensa, o ministro dos Transportes, Oscar Puente, revelou que houve um problema de comunicação no computador, que fez com que os trens fossem imediatamente parados e o erro ocorreu na retomada das operações.

"A decisão de reiniciar a viagem do trem não foi tomada como deveria, em um ritmo que permitisse a sua parada. Um sinal vermelho estava em vigor, proibindo qualquer movimento adicional. Apesar disso, o trem da Renfe recebeu ordem para retomar sua viagem e prosseguiu até a colisão", declarou.

Segundo a porta-voz do governo local, da região de Castilla La Mancha, Ester Padilla, o trem da Renfe, com 397 pessoas a bordo, e o trem da Iryo, com 147 passageiros, colidiram pouco depois das 9h do horário local - 5h de Brasília -, entre as cidades de Mora e Orgaz, causando o descarrilamento de vagões.

Imagens aéreas mostram vagões descarrilados — Foto: Guarda Civil / Divulgação

As duas empresas ainda não responderam aos pedidos de comentários da Reuters, e a circulação ferroviária está interrompida entre Madrid , Ciudad Real e Andalucía.

Equipes resgatam vítimas de colisão entre trens de alta velocidade em Urda, na Espanha, no dia 28 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Juanma Jiménez/Europa Press/AP

Depoimentos mostram gravidade do acidente

Miguel, um passageiro que viajava com vários colegas no último vagão de um dos trens, descreveu à rádio COPE o momento do acidente:

"Ouvimos um estrondo enorme, um baque realmente gigantesco que durou 10 segundos, como se o trem estivesse prestes a descarrilar. Pela janela da direita, pudemos ver um trem destruído – imagino que deva ter sido o outro".

Eduarda, passageira do trem Iryo, contou à rádio Cadena SER que sentiu um forte impacto que a jogou para a frente, fazendo-a pensar inicialmente que o trem havia feito uma parada de emergência. Ela só se deu conta da gravidade do acidente depois de ver pessoas feridas e ser orientada a evacuar o local.

"Eu vi pessoas mortas", contou ela, ao relembrar que viu o que descreveu como uma cena catastrófica, com parte do trem pendurada na encosta e um incêndio em um dos vagões após descer um barranco em segurança.

Jesús Pérez Martín, prefeito da cidade vizinha de Los Yébenes, disse que a situação é "horrível" e a classificou como uma grave tragédia.

"Eles estão me contando sobre mutilações e ferimentos muito graves", disse ele à RTVE.

A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, ao tomar conhecimento do acidente, afirmou que "hoje a Europa chora".

O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, classificou a tragédia como um "terrível drama ferroviário".

Em nota, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Brasil lamentou o acidente:

"O Brasil manifesta sua solidariedade ao povo e ao governo da Espanha, transmite suas sinceras condolências às famílias das vítimas e deseja pronta recuperação aos feridos. articles.summary: Ricardo Leandro Rodrigues, de 20 anos, quebrou a bacia após ser atingido em cheio por um veículo quando estava a caminho de uma entrega na noite de terça-feira (27).
articles.body:
Um motociclista que sofreu um acidente na noite de terça-feira (27), em Ribeirão Preto (SP), aguardou por 12 horas até ser transferido de uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) para um hospital, segundo a família.

Ricardo Leandro Rodrigues, de 20 anos, quebrou a bacia após ser atingido em cheio por um veículo quando estava a caminho de uma entrega. A batida aconteceu na Rua Espírito Santo, no bairro Ipiranga, e foi flagrada por câmeras de segurança.

O motorista que atingiu em Ricardo se preparava para fazer a curva e entrar na garagem de uma casa. Nas imagens, é possível ver que, com o impacto, o motociclista foi arremessado para a calçada e bateu em uma árvore. A queda foi amortecida pela bag que ele utilizava.

À EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, a mãe do jovem, Daniela dos Reis Borges, disse que foi comunicada de que a vaga para o filho saiu na Santa Casa por volta das 22h, mas a transferência não foi feita. Segundo ela, Ricardo reclamava de dor e, em alguns momentos, ficou sem medicamento.

O jovem foi transferido para o hospital na manhã desta quarta-feira (28).

"A vaga dele saiu às 22h37 da noite de ontem. Então, ele veio sofrendo dor, não colocaram nenhum soro depois nele, ele ficou sem medicação. Só agora, por volta de 6h da manhã, que deu medicação. Então, deu 12 horas sem ambulância. Quando eu saí lá fora, perguntei para a ambulância do Samu, eles chegavam com os pacientes e iam embora vazio. Está precário, tem 12 pessoas já com o hospital, mas não tem ambulância para buscar".

Procurada pela EPTV , a Secretaria Municipal da Saúde informou que a a transferência ocorreu assim que um leito foi liberado na Santa Casa.

"O paciente deu entrada na UPA Oeste às 19h07 de ontem, via SAMU, após acidente entre moto e carro na Rua Espírito Santo, no Ipiranga. Foi atendido no setor vermelho e submetido a exame de raio-X, que identificou uma fratura. Foi solicitada regulação médica em vaga zero. Embora estável, o paciente permaneceu sob cuidados da equipe da UPA Oeste, recebendo medicação para dor, até a efetiva disponibilização do leito. A transferência ocorreu assim que o leito foi liberado pela Santa Casa".

Ainda segundo a Secretaria de Saúde, as ambulâncias que estavam paradas na UPA, e foram alvo de reclamação por parte da mãe do motociclista, são para atendimento de ocorrências nas ruas, dentro da rotina normal do serviço de urgência.

"Após cada transporte de paciente, os veículos passam por limpeza e desinfecção, conforme os protocolos de biossegurança e os Procedimentos Operacionais Padrão (POP) do serviço de saúde".

articles.title: Canada signs trade deal with UAE in push for non-US markets
articles.summary: The agreement aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access for businesses in both countries.
articles.body:
Canada and the United Arab Emirates have signed a comprehensive trade deal to lower barriers between the economies and boost investment, the governments have said.

The deal comes as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties amid tension with the United States.

Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan presided over the signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) on Tuesday, which aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access for businesses in both countries.

Carney has pledged to double Ottawa’s non-US trade over the next decade as US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have rippled through Canada’s economy.

Subsequent attempts to reach a deal with Washington have broken down, which has pushed Carney to aggressively pursue trade pacts with countries from the Asia Pacific to Europe and the Middle East.

“Once fully implemented, the CEPA will reduce or eliminate tariffs on over 99 percent of current Canadian exports to the UAE,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a statement.

“That means new markets for Canadian farmers growing pulses and canola, for manufacturers of industrial machinery and power generation equipment, for our world-class aerospace sector, and other Canadian innovators.”

“The agreement will also address non-tariff barriers, create a more predictable environment for trade and investment, and expand market access for Canadian goods and services, including in the industrial, agricultural, forest, fish and seafood, environmental, and engineering sectors,” it said, adding that CEPA is expected to enter into force in 2027.

The two countries also signed preliminary agreements on energy, diplomatic and defence cooperation.

“We see considerable potential for our private sector, whether through improved market access for our exporters or access to investment opportunities in high-growth sectors such as logistics, communications, advanced technology and manufacturing – all of which will support our pursuit of a resilient, diversified and globally connected economy,” the UAE’s Foreign Trade Minister Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi said in a statement.

He signed the CEPA deal with his Canadian counterpart, Maninder Sidhu.

The UAE is the largest Middle East market for Canadian exports and a major buyer of Canadian motor vehicles and parts, and machinery.

Two-way trade between the countries was worth 3.5 billion Canadian dollars ($2.48bn) last year. It has been growing at 10 percent annually for the last few years, according to government data.

The UAE also committed up to $50bn in investment in Canada last year.

articles.title: Court orders closure of one of Egypt’s last independent media outlets
articles.summary: An Egyptian court ordered the closure of one of Egypt’s last independent news outlets Tuesday after convicting its editor-in-chief of operating a website without a license, a major blow to the country’s shrinking press freedom.
articles.body: An Egyptian court ordered the closure of one of Egypt’s last independent news outlets Tuesday after convicting its editor-in-chief of operating a website without a license, a major blow to the country’s shrinking press freedom. The publication, Mada Masr, said its editor-in-chief and founder, Lina Attalah, was released after paying a fine equivalent to about $53,400. She had been detained for seven hours after the verdict, with her whereabouts unknown during that time, according to the outlet. Mada Masr is one of the few remaining news outlets in Egypt known for investigating corruption, the expanding role of the country’s powerful military, and human rights violations in a country where newspapers and television stations are closely controlled by authorities. Ahead of Tuesday’s hearing, Human Rights Watch called the prosecution of Attalah an escalation of an “outrageous attack on independent media.” Attalah’s lead lawyer, Hassan el-Azhary, said Mada Masr planned to appeal the closure order. “Today’s decision represents a crushing blow to press freedom in Egypt and marks a dark day for independent journalism in the country,” Amnesty International said in a statement. By imposing a large fine, ordering the closure of Mada Masr and the seizure of its property, while “detaining Lina Attalah until payment is made, the Egyptian authorities are sending a clear and ruthless message: critical, independent reporting will not be tolerated.” While completing her release paperwork, Attalah’s defense team learned that the 44-year-old journalist had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of spreading false news and operating an unlicensed website — a conviction she intends to appeal, according to Mada Masr’s Facebook page. An appeal hearing is set for Nov 11. During Tuesday’s session at a Cairo misdemeanor court — the first in a trial announced last week — the judge rejected all of the defense’s procedural requests and ordered its lawyers to immediately give closing arguments, said Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, a rights group, who attended the session. When Attalah’s eight lawyers refused, the judge brought in a court-appointed lawyer none of them knew, over loud objections from the defense and from Attalah herself, Bahgat said. The judge declined to enter her rejection of the lawyer into the record, he said. State security prosecutors summoned Attalah for questioning last week on charges of publishing false news and operating without a license, then referred her to trial on the latter charge. Mada Masr says it first applied for a license in 2018 but never received an answer. Authorities have blocked its website inside Egypt since 2017, and the outlet says this is the sixth case brought against it or its journalists in six years. Amnesty International and 118 other civil society groups and independent media outlets worldwide called on Egyptian authorities to stop targeting Mada Masr and grant it a license. Khaled Elbalshy, head of the Egyptian Journalists Syndicate, the country’s press union, said in a Facebook post that the organization is standing by and supporting Attalah’s case, calling it “a wake-up call” that “runs counter to the demands” for removing press restrictions and media reform. The case comes amid a broader crackdown on independent media in Egypt. On Tuesday, Egyptian prosecutors extended for another 15 days the pre-trial detention of all six journalists of the Matsadaash investigative platform, according to a statement posted on the platform’s Facebook page. “Their detention was extended without any new questioning, without being asked to respond to the accusations against them, and without being presented with any evidence to substantiate those allegations,” read the statement. In late September, Matsadaash reporters were arrested on grounds of joining and financing a terrorist group and spreading false information — a generic list of charges brought against journalists and political critics in recent years. Egypt ranks 169th among 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders’ 2026 World Press Freedom Index.

images.caption: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, co-founder and editor-in-chief of the Cairo-based online newspaper Mada Masr, gives an interview with AFP in the capital Cairo on December 28, 2020.

articles.title: Train crash in Spain kills at least 68 people
articles.summary: Crash occurs near Urda in Toledo province, south of Madrid, on high-speed line connecting the capital with Seville.
articles.body:
A high-speed train has crashed into the rear of another train that had stopped in central Spain, derailing two carriages and killing at least 68 people, the regional government says.

Emiliano Garcia-Page, the government head for the Castilla-La Mancha region, where the crash happened, said about 80 people were injured, about 50 of them seriously and 15 critically, warning that some of the most seriously injured might not survive. Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said the injured were being taken to several hospitals in the area.

The crash occurred early on Wednesday near Urda in Toledo province, south of Madrid, on a high-speed railway line connecting the capital with the southern city of Seville.

Esther Padilla, a spokeswoman for the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, told Spanish public broadcaster TVE that the trains had been travelling in the same direction when one struck the rear of the other, which was stationary, causing two carriages to derail.

The collision involved an AVE high-speed train operated by Spain’s state railway company Renfe, travelling from Madrid to Seville, and another operated by the private rail company Iryo.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, speaking from Urda, said the government would declare three days of official mourning from October 29 to 31.

“Spain is in mourning,” he said. “We will get to the bottom of this, and if there was negligence, it will be revealed, and if there were system failures, there will be a strong response.” He added: “What is unacceptable for a country like Spain is to suffer two train accidents in the same year,” but said the causes of the two crashes appeared unrelated.

More than 200 members of the Military Emergencies Unit are working at the site, and the town council of Los Yebenes says it has gathered food and basic supplies for those affected.

Journalist Graham Keeley, speaking to Al Jazeera from Spain, said the crash “comes at an awful time for the present government because we have an election here in Spain in just over a month.”

“After the crash in January, the government promised to conduct checks on all the lines all over the country,” he said, adding that passengers on board were commuters travelling from Madrid to Seville, along with tourists.

The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators and on the same line that killed 46 people.

Footage circulating on social media showed the wreckage from one of the carriages scattered along a slope after it derailed, with members of the public and rescue crews gathered around it.

Padilla said 397 passengers were on the Renfe train and 147 on the Iryo train.

Two carriages of the Iryo train fell down an embankment, according to emergency service sources quoted by the newspaper El Pais.

Health Minister Garcia told TVE that emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and recovering bodies from the two most damaged train cars.

“It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy,” Garcia said.

Spain’s Transport Minister Oscar Puente said at a press conference that a control centre decision allowed a train to resume its journey “normally” despite a signaling system failure.

Puente told journalists that the LZB control system went down at around 8:30am (07:00 GMT) along a 63km (39-mile) stretch, affecting six trains, though he said the exact number was not certain. With the system down, control was transferred to the Atocha control post, where the decision was made for the Renfe train to resume its journey “normally”.

“The decision to resume traffic without the system having been restored corresponds to the control centre,” Puente said, describing the circumstances as “inexplicable”.

Madrid Mayor Jose Luis Martinez-Almeida said on X that the capital was also sending emergency medical teams and firefighters to assist with rescue efforts.

Spain’s railway infrastructure operator, ADIF, suspended high-speed rail services between Madrid and the southern region of Andalusia while the Civil Guard sent a disaster investigation team to the site, El Pais reported.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on X that he was shocked by the incident and remained in contact with Transport Minister Puente and Castilla-La Mancha administrator Garcia-Page as emergency crews worked at the scene.

“Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families,” Sanchez said.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she was devastated by the news and extended condolences to the victims’ families and loved ones.

“Today, Europe mourns with you,” she said in a post on X.

French President Emmanuel Macron expressed solidarity with Spain, saying his thoughts were with the victims, their families, the injured, and rescue workers.

articles.body: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu Environment and Climate Change Minister Dr V K Rajiv has sparked widespread debate after claiming that household wastewater, rather than industrial discharge, is responsible for foam in rivers.The controversy began during his visit to Tirupur, where he remarked that domestic soaps and shampoos were the primary causes of river frothing. Following heavy online backlash, the minister issued a clarification at the Chennai Secretariat. Defending his credentials, Rajiv said the chief minister had appointed him because of his medical background and emphasised his efforts to modernise the department. He asserted that recent statewide water studies had confirmed that industrial effluents were not to blame. Instead, he explained that domestic greywater containing high levels of phosphorus from soaps and shampoos naturally creates foam when it mixes with river water.Strongly condemning the minister’s remarks, AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran slammed the government for deflecting responsibility onto ordinary citizens. articles.title: Spain train crash leaves at least 64 dead in second major collision this year
articles.summary: BARCELONA, Spain — At least 68 people were killed and 68 injured when two high-speed trains collided in central Spain on Wednesday, sending carriages careering off the tracks, in the second major accident on the same line in less than a year.
articles.body: BARCELONA, Spain — At least 68 people were killed and 68 injured when two high-speed trains collided in central Spain on Wednesday, sending carriages careering off the tracks, in the second major accident on the same line in less than a year. “We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail,” one passenger, Miguel, told Spain’s COPE radio, adding that he was traveling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains. “Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train — I imagine it must have been the other one,” he added. Pictures showed several carriages lying on their sides next to the tracks and others twisted at angles, their wheels sheared off. Debris was strewn around the scene of the accident in the countryside in the province of Toledo. As rescue teams continued to search through the wreckage ‌of ​the ‌derailed ⁠carriages, the Castilla-La Mancha ‌regional government said ‌68 people had been killed and 68 injured. Together the two trains were carrying more than 500 passengers. “The government of Spain and the whole state are with the victims and also with the families of the victims,” Prime Minister of Spain Pedro Sánchez said at the site of the crash on Wednesday. Sánchez, who is facing a snap election next month, said the government was investigating the cause of the crash and any failures, vowing action “if there has been negligence.” He said that the country must restore confidence in its high-speed rail network, with the crash coming after a separate disaster on the same rail line killed 46 people in January. “It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to have two high-speed accidents in less than a year,” he said. Spain’s transport minister Oscar Puente said Wednesday’s crash ⁠occurred after a state-owned Renfe high-speed train was authorized ⁠to ​continue its ⁠journey despite an active red ⁠signal and ⁠a stationary ‌train from private rail company Iryo on the tracks ahead. Addressing ‌reporters in ‌Madrid, Puente said ⁠the red signal was issued due to a computer communications failure which automatically stopped ‌traffic. An erroneous ​decision was ‌made ⁠to restart the ⁠Renfe train, breaking protocol, he said. Locals rushed to the scene of the accident, which has prompted a major national emergency response and raised questions about the safety and security of Spain’s high-speed rail infrastructure, which had previously been hailed as among the most sophisticated in Europe. Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the Castilla La Mancha region, told state broadcaster TVE that the trains were heading in the same direction from Madrid to Seville when one ran into the tail of the other, which had stopped on the line. She added that some 397 people had been traveling on the Renfe train and 147 people on the Iryo train. Spain’s royal family who said they shared “in the grief of the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives.” Spanish political parties said Wednesday they would briefly pause campaigning ahead of next month’s general election. Spain’s football federation also said it would postpone some of its Copa del Rey soccer fixtures, following the collision. Juan Manuel Moreno, the president of the Andalusian regional government, said on X that there would be three days of mourning in the region. The full scale of the disaster remains unclear but officials said an emergency phone line had been set up for families of the victims; local blood banks had also made appeals for donations. Manuel Galan, the mayor of the nearby municipality of Urda, said he had been asked by emergency services to prepare a sports hall to accommodate the injured. Eduarda, a passenger on the Iryo train, told Spain’s Cadena SER radio that she felt a strong impact that threw her forward and she initially thought the train had made an emergency stop. After climbing down an embankment to safety, she said she saw part of the train hanging down the slope and a fire in one carriage. “I saw dead people,” she added. Salvador Arriza, a 62-year-old employee of Airbus, was travelling to the rear of the Renfe train. He told the Reuters news agency the carriage ended up “completely wrecked, with seats being ripped out.” “I was lucky because I was in a backward-facing seat, and the impact pushed me into it,” he added. “After the first hit I was disoriented, but the worst thing was that the train then kept moving for quite some time from the inertia and that’s when I thought something would happen to me.” Emergency responders, including a helicopter, police and ambulances, arrived within about 20 minutes, she said. Spain has the largest high-speed rail network in Europe for trains moving more than 155 mph, with more than 1,900 miles of track, according to the European Union.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors: Joe Lycett's tribute to viral TikTok Tonteg gran
articles.summary: Anne Hughes found fame after being hoisted into the air after getting caught in shop shutters.
articles.body:
Celebrity Traitors star and comedian Joe Lycett has paid colourful tribute to the Welsh grandmother who went viral on TikTok after getting caught in shop shutters and being hoisted into the air.

The moment Anne Hughes was left dangling 7ft (2.1 metres) in the air was captured on CCTV - and viewed tens of millions of times on social media.

Lycett, who is also an artist and a fan of the viral video, painted the incident for his art exhibition at the Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery.

Anne died in 2025 , but her granddaughter, Lilly Hughes, said Lycett's "lovely" painting has meant her nan's legacy has lived on and she would "have it on my wall any day".

The Everything Must Go exhibition is Lycett's first major solo art exhibition and is "about things which are no longer with us".

Lycett, who was banished from Celebrity Traitors for being too keen to be a traitor, said on Instagram: "My painting in tribute to the great Anne Hughes, who brought joy to millions when she was hoisted into the air outside the best-one she worked at in Rhondda Cynon Taf, Wales.

"She took the experience in good spirit, saying in an interview with the BBC, 'my grandchildren ask me why I am holding on to my trolley and I say I just don't know'."

Anne's interviews with BBC Wales and footage from the famous CCTV ended up being viewed at least 58 million times on the BBC News Instagram account alone.

Lilly, 28, who was very close to her grandmother, said: "I thought she's back from the dead, she's risen again and now my nan is in a museum.

"It's lovely, I would have it on my wall any day."

In the past 12 months, Lycett, 38, from Birmingham, has been producing works the museum has described as celebrating "nostalgia, grief and loss", from a sculpture of an extinct large woolly mammoth to an abstract painting of TV personality Cilla Black, who died in 2015.

The artwork, including Anne's moment, are painted in a child-like style and in bold and bright colours.

Lilly said her grandmother's legacy has lived on. She said: "Every time that it's mentioned people laugh about it. And then it just brings a smile to my face because I think 'oh nan, if you were here today'.

"It's absolutely hilarious, so it definitely helps with the grieving process."

The viral moment was previously immortalised by graffiti artist Tee2Sugars on the shutter she was caught on.

Lilly, who is a midwife and lives in Caerphilly, added: "Honestly if she was alive today she would say that the world has gone mad. I find Joe really funny and the fact that he's now painted my nan is a bit mind-blowing."

She also revealed her grandmother had told a "little fib" in her BBC interview about holding onto her trolley, and said she was in fact holding onto it because "she didn't want anyone stealing her fags".

Lilly says she still uses the story as an "ice breaker" in her work.

"I'll be looking after a woman and I will tell her about my nan and all of sudden I'm in the room with her whole family watching the video and they'll be absolutely peeing themselves. It's brilliant," she said.

articles.title: Rajnath, Hegseth review 10-year defence pact, explore tech sharing, reaffirm commitment to eliminate terrorism
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union defence minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday held a meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union defence minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday held a meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in the Philippine city of Cebu to review the progress of the Indo-US defence partnership.“Both leaders also reviewed the progress of the 10-year India-US Defence Framework and concluded by reaffirming their shared commitment to further elevate the India-US defence relationship to strategic convergence,” a defence ministry’s release said on Wednesday.The discussions touched upon advancing military-to-military exchanges, augmenting maritime security collaboration, and integrating robust defence supply chains to further deepen and expand ongoing defence industry collaboration, it said.Reflecting on the ongoing collaboration, both sides noted the robust progression of their foundational security agreements and explored fresh pathways to accelerate operational readiness, technology sharing and defence industrial integration.A key highlight of the dialogue was the review of regional security, during which both nations strongly emphasised their joint resolve to eliminate the global menace of terrorism. Rajnath stressed that the global community must maintain an uncompromising, zero-tolerance approach towards nations that support, train or fund terrorist organisations.Secretary Hegseth reaffirmed the US’s unwavering solidarity and full support to India in its fight against cross-border terrorism. Rajnath expressed India's deep appreciation for the consistent and strong support extended by the US.In their wide-ranging talks, Rajnath and Hegseth also reviewed the situation in the Indo-Pacific and fast-evolving regional security dynamics. After the talks, Rajnath posted on X, “Had an excellent meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of the 13th ADMM-Plus. We reviewed the progress of our 10-year India-US Defence Framework... Our robust partnership continues to be a cornerstone for a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific.”India and the US continue to expand their strategic defence partnership after the 10-year framework was signed in late 2025. The US granted India ‘Major Defence Partner (MDP)’ status in June 2016 to streamline access to advanced military hardware and technology transfers.Over the years, the two countries have signed several defence and security pacts to boost defence coordination and cooperation. The key ones among them are the Logistics Exchange Memorandum of Agreement (LEMOA) in 2016 for using each other's bases for repair and replenishment of supplies; the Communications Compatibility and Security Agreement in 2018 for providing interoperability between the two militaries and the sale of high-end technology from the US to India; and the BECA (Basic Exchange and Cooperation Agreement) in 2020 to bolster bilateral defence ties. BECA provides for the sharing of high-end military technology, logistics and geospatial maps between the two countries.

articles.title: Burnham’s government unveils its first UK budget: What to expect
articles.summary: UK chancellor to present an autumn budget amid rising living costs and energy bills.
articles.body:
British Chancellor John Healey will set out the country’s autumn budget, the government’s tax and spending plans, the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s premiership amid high inflation and government spending levels.

While the budget will be announced in parliament on Wednesday at 12.30 GMT, speculation about what it will lay out has ranged from a series of tax announcements to commitments to defence spending.

But the country continues to deal with a rising cost-of-living crisis and energy bills are expected to see their biggest rise in four years in January due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

As total United Kingdom borrowing broke through the 3 trillion pounds ($3.99 trillion) barrier for the first time in September, the country is already spending 100 billion pounds ($133bn) each year just on servicing that debt.

Despite that challenge, the chancellor has said the budget will move “money and power out of Westminster and into every postcode around Britain”.

In a speech last month, Healey said that he and Burnham were in “lockstep” in meeting fiscal rules, “to balancing the books, with a buffer to protect against uncertainty, to control borrowing to bear down on inflation, and reducing long-term pressures on our public finances”.

Gregory Thwaites, interim chief economist at the British think tank, Resolution Foundation, told Al Jazeera he is expecting a “relatively small budget given the limited room for maneuvre the government has”.

“A bit of action to offset high living costs,” but “most big decisions postponed to next year.”

Following the two budgets from former Chancellor Rachel Reeves, which included big tax and spending increases, Healey’s budget is expected to take a more “steady as she goes” line, which some say is the wrong approach.

Here’s how he will be expected to achieve that.

On Monday, Burnham said Healey would set out a plan to fully fund the government’s defence plans and commitments, telling ITV’s Good Morning Britain that his government’s first challenge was financing the already announced defence investment plan.

Announced in June, the plan is backed by 298 billion pounds ($396bn) of investment and will transform the armed forces as the country moves to “warfighting readiness” and stepping up “European security”, according to a government policy paper.

But Burnham said it was “crucial that we have a funded plan that we can then implement, and we will set out more details on Wednesday as to how we’ve done that”.

He added that NATO commitments of spending 3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) on defence spending by 2030 and 3.5 percent by 2035 are included in the pathway, explaining that national security issues were “at the top of the priority list”.

As it stands, Britain spends about 2.6 percent of its GDP on defence.

The Guardian reported that on defence spending, Healey aims to close a 4.7-billion-pound ($6.2bn) funding gap in the government’s plan inherited from the previous Labour Party leader, with cuts to other departmental budgets likely to fund it.

Government borrowing and inflation continue to rise, which is a potential spanner in the works for proposed spending.

Last week, UK inflation and government borrowing both hit their highest levels in a year.

According to the Office for National Statistics, borrowing was nearly 25 billion pounds ($33bn) last month alone, “a little higher than a year earlier, as spending, including higher debt interest costs, increased more than government income, partly reflecting the impacts of inflation”.

ONS added that in the financial year to September 2026, borrowing remained below the same period last year, but it was higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecast.

According to Jasper Kenter, a professorial research fellow in ecological economics at Aberystwyth Business School, for the government to grow the economy without raising inflation levels, there needs to be an understanding of what kind of economy is created.

“The strongest policies improve prosperity, resilience and sustainability at the same time,” Kenter said.

“Growth is less likely to be inflationary when it comes from increasing the economy’s productive capacity rather than simply boosting spending. Measures that improve skills, reduce energy dependence, strengthen local economies and regenerate ecosystems are likely to deliver more lasting benefits than short-term stimulus,” he added.

Moreover, Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said in a media release ahead of the budget that Healey “faces a forecast in which borrowing is still expected to fall in coming years, and the fiscal rules are still being met”.

“Despite that, a ‘steady-as-she-goes’ budget is not an option available to the chancellor. Choosing to stay the course with the inherited tax and spending plans would mean allowing inflation to blow departments’ spending plans off course,” Miller said.

The budget is also expected to reveal new taxes on banks and online marketplaces such as Amazon, Temu and eBay, as well as a funding boost for mayoralties and local authorities.

The biggest four banks collectively made about profits of 15 billion pounds ($19.9bn) in the first six months of this year. Trade unions are calling for higher taxes on those earnings, the BBC has reported.

According to the BBC, the Treasury is leaning towards changing a 2023 surcharge rate on banks, which would raise about 2 billion pounds ($2.6bn).

On marketplaces such as Amazon, Healey is reportedly looking to crack down on foreign sellers who avoid paying VAT – a UK sales tax – which is expected to raise as much as 1 billion pounds ($1.3bn) and help fund business rate cuts for high street shops, The Times reported.

According to The Guardian newspaper, Healey is expected to allocate about 1.42 trillion pounds ($1.8 trillion) this year for day-to-day spending and public investment, with about 100 billion pounds ($132.8bn) going on debt interest.

Kenter, of Aberystwyth Business School, told Al Jazeera that he expects “targeted support rather than large-scale tax cuts or rises” in the budget announcement.

“The government appears keen to signal empathy with the pressures many people are facing. Addressing the harsh cliff edge in carer’s allowance and expanding parental pay are good examples of this,” he said.

Some of the budget’s contents have already been announced, including ending the carers’ allowance limit and removing tariffs on a range of food items, including chocolate and beans, to make them cheaper for shoppers.

Pensioners are also expected to be shielded from income tax through the introduction of a new personal allowance, while Healey is expected to add another 1 billion pounds ($1.3bn) to the 39 billion pounds ($51.8bn) planned for social and affordable housing in England over the next decade.

“Pensioners will benefit from another substantial increase in the state pension, while low-paid workers will benefit from increases in the minimum wage. For most households, the bigger determinants of living standards will remain wages, inflation and energy costs rather than any new tax measures announced in the budget,” Kenter explained.

Last month, Burnham announced a new national care service to provide free personal care for elderly people. As costs of care for the elderly have soared in the UK, this was a major issue from the outset of Burnham’s premiership.

He said the plan would be introduced in phases and would be fully funded from public spending and savings from scrapping the state pension triple lock – an annual increase in state pension that goes up with inflation, wages or a fixed rate of 2.5 percent, whichever is highest.

A report on how this will be implemented is due in summer 2027.

Amid high gas and oil prices as a result of the US-Israeli war with Iran and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz, energy prices worldwide have increased, with Brent crude futures at $115.90 a barrel on Wednesday.

In the UK, energy prices are predicted to reach nearly 2,000 pounds ($2,655) a year for households in January after energy consultancy Cornwall Insight projected in its latest forecast last month that the government’s cap on energy prices is expected to increase by 16 percent.

On energy bills, reports suggest the chancellor is expected to announce help for households in the budget by scrapping standing charges for energy supply, among other things.

articles.title: An 18-year-old fisherman went out to sea with his cousin; 41 days later, rescuers found him alone in the Pacific, 2,000 km from home
articles.summary: An 18-year-old fisherman from Papua New Guinea has been rescued after spending 41 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean, thousands of kilometres from home.
articles.body: An 18-year-old fisherman from Papua New Guinea has been rescued after spending 41 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean, thousands of kilometres from home. Luka Rahan had set out on a fishing trip with his cousin when their boat developed engine trouble, leaving them at the mercy of the sea. With no anchor to secure the vessel, the boat drifted across the Pacific before a group of fishermen from Kiribati spotted it near the islands of Tarawa and Maiana. Rahan was found alone and severely dehydrated, while his cousin had reportedly died about a week before the rescue. Taken to a hospital in Kiribati's capital, Tarawa, the teenager began recovering as news of his extraordinary ordeal reached his home country.A fishing trip turned into a 41-day ordealRahan, from northern Bougainville in Papua New Guinea, had ventured out to sea with his cousin when their boat developed engine problems. Without a functioning engine and an anchor to keep the vessel in place, the pair were left drifting in open water.Their boat travelled an estimated 2,000 kilometres from their starting point before reaching waters between Tarawa and Maiana, part of the island nation of Kiribati. The journey left the teenager far from home, with no immediate access to help.After 41 days at sea, local fishermen spotted the boat on October 27 and discovered Rahan alone. His rescue brought an end to an ordeal that had left him severely dehydrated and in need of medical care.His cousin reportedly died before the rescueRahan's cousin, who had accompanied him on the fishing trip, reportedly died at sea approximately a week before the teenager was found. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been fully detailed in the reports.By the time the fishermen reached the boat, Rahan was alone. His survival came amid the loss of his travelling companion, turning the rescue into a story of both extraordinary endurance and tragedy.A fellow Papua New Guinean helped him recoverFollowing the rescue, Rahan was taken to a hospital in Tarawa, Kiribati's capital, for treatment. He was severely dehydrated, but reports said he was responsive and gradually regaining his strength.Jonathan Anthony Kunau, a Papua New Guinean engineer living and working in Tarawa, visited the teenager after learning about his rescue. Kunau wanted to ensure that Rahan was receiving care and did not feel alone while recovering in a foreign country.He also helped establish contact with Rahan's family in Papua New Guinea, informing them that the teenager had been found alive. The news brought relief to relatives who had been waiting to learn his fate.Another long-distance rescue involving fishermen from BougainvilleRahan's rescue came after another incident involving people from Bougainville who were found near Kiribati following an extended period adrift at sea.In that earlier case, three people from Nissan Island reportedly spent around 70 days drifting before being rescued. They later returned home. The incidents have drawn attention to the risks faced by people travelling in small boats across the Pacific, where engine failures and the absence of suitable safety equipment can leave vessels vulnerable to winds and ocean currents.A reminder of the risks of travelling at seaRahan's ordeal highlights how quickly a routine fishing trip can become a life-threatening emergency when a vessel loses power far from shore. An anchor can help prevent a boat from drifting in some conditions, while reliable navigation equipment and emergency communication devices can improve the chances of getting assistance.Kunau urged fishermen to carry essential equipment, including a compass, an anchor and a phone. For those travelling beyond mobile network coverage, suitable marine communication equipment is also important.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Texas’ Senate candidates rally at dueling events just a few miles apart. No clear winner in Israeli election but Netanyahu looks far from defeated. And a new CDC report warns of rising threat of drug-resistant germs. Here’s what to know today. James Talarico faces off against Trump in dueling Texas rallies In reliably red Lubbock, Texas, people waited for hours in lines that stretched for blocks to see Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Less than three miles away, a similar scene unfolded for President Donald Trump, as he sought to boost the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton. This is Morning Rundown, a weekday newsletter to start your day. Sign up here to get it in your inbox. Yesterday’s dueling rallies in the city, which has a population of less than 300,000, underscored the high stakes in a Senate race that could see the Republican Party lose its grip on Texas. At Talarico’s rally, Democrats panned the economy, high gas prices and closures of rural hospitals. The Senate candidate called Paxton corrupt and sought to tie him to Elon Musk, who has significant business interests in the state. For Trump and Paxton, the stop in Lubbock was their second of the day, having held an earlier rally in Corpus Christi. At the evening event, Trump cast Talarico as a Second Amendment-hating, meat-loathing extremist out of touch with everyday Texans. Paxton leaned on Trump’s support, calling him “the greatest president of my lifetime.” And in a potential sign that Republicans were looking to attract more voters, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has generally held higher approval ratings than others in the administration, was given a speaking part. Trump announced plans to undo Biden-era regulations on methane, the second-biggest contributor to climate change after carbon dioxide. A federal grand jury declined to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, the former Trump White House aide turned star Jan. 6 witness. Israel’s election has no clear winner — but Netanyahu looks far from defeated again When Israelis awoke on Wednesday, it seemed that their future had taken another twist overnight: Results that had looked like a narrow loss for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when they went to bed now pointed to a narrow lead by dawn. There is still no obvious winner, with uncertainty set to follow the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023. The votes are still being counted, and Israel’s Central Elections Commission said final results likely won’t be known until tomorrow. But the preliminary tallies from this pivotal contest still point to one clear outcome: Netanyahu suffered significant losses but he didn’t really lose. Still, the Israeli public dealt Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister for nearly 20 of the past 30 years, a notable electoral setback. With more than 84% of the votes counted, Netanyahu’s coalition, the most right-wing in Israeli history, would be diminished from 64 members to only 54, short of the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government. He appears to have eked out a slight advantage over the bloc led by his main rival, former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, in contrast to the initial projection from exit polls on Tuesday night. Each leader claimed to have received a mandate from voters but stopped short of claiming victory. Read more about what could happen next. Interest rates expected to hold steady ahead of midterms The Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates unchanged today despite climbing inflation. With less than a week to go until Election Day, economic experts expect the Fed to keep its tradition of staying far away from politics, especially as rising prices are set to play a key role in the polls. The Fed last month raised rates by a quarter of a percentage point. Inflation figures for September, released this month, show the annual rate rose to 3.7% from 3.4% the previous month, which some experts feel is reason enough to hike rates. CDC warns of rising threat of drug-resistant germs A new CDC report sheds light on what the agency calls one of the nation’s most urgent public health threats: infections resistant to existing treatments, which kill more than 50,000 people in the U.S. each year. The new report — the first comprehensive assessment of these pathogens in seven years — estimated that 19 drug-resistant germs cause 9.7 million infections annually in the U.S. Of them, four were ranked as the most worrisome, including the bacteria that causes gonorrhea, which has become resistant to all but one class of antibiotics used to treat it. Its remoteness is a reason why some of the 1,800 detainees say they feel isolated and forgotten. During visiting hours, we met with a man who offered a first-hand account of what life was like inside. He spoke about some physical hardships but mostly about his mental-health struggles. Being held in a facility so far away from legal representation and his loved ones, he said, made him feel alone and forgotten. articles.title: British university student turns her pet rats into viral miniature artists, selling their paintings for up to £50 to help fund her degree
articles.summary: A university student from Droitwich has found an unusual way to help fund her studies by selling miniature paintings created by her pet rats.
articles.body: A university student from Droitwich has found an unusual way to help fund her studies by selling miniature paintings created by her pet rats. Ella Woodland, who studies at the University of Worcester, began selling the tiny artworks after a video of her rats painting went viral on social media, attracting around 6 million views.According to the BBC, Woodland now lists about 16 pieces of rat-made art each week. Each painting sells for £15, while some larger pieces have fetched up to £50. Buyers have also requested the artworks as birthday presents, and one buyer even asked for a wedding gift.How Ella Woodland turned her pet rats into miniature artistsElla Woodland began selling paintings made by her pet rats last February, after sharing a video of them creating artwork online. The idea came after she watched a similar creator's video on Facebook and decided to try it with her own animals.Woodland said, "I tried it with them and then I posted it, and then somebody else shared it, and it went viral that way”"They got six million views, I think”"Then I started getting loads of followers on Vinted from that."Her online following has helped turn their small paintings into a source of income while she studies at the University of Worcester.The simple technique behind Woodland’s rat paintingsWoodland said, "I put some paint in a little playpen for them and they follow a trail of baby food across my finger and across the canvas, and that's just how I get them to paint”.She said the rats have become more adventurous outside their cage since they started the activity; they now spend more time outside it.Woodland also gives them plenty of treats after their painting sessions. She believes they are happy taking part in the activity.Woodland’s rat paintings attract buyers and help fund her university expensesWoodland currently sells each painting for £15, while some larger pieces have sold for about £50. She lists approximately 16 pieces of artwork each week, providing an additional source of income to help cover her university expenses.The paintings have attracted buyers looking for unusual gifts. Many customers request the tiny creations for birthdays, while one buyer wanted a painting as a wedding present. The wedding gift was to feature the colours associated with the event.Woodland said, "I think my family have been fascinated by it”"It's wowed people how big they've got and how it's very unusual, so I think people are just shocked by it."How rat paintings became part of Woodland’s lifeDespite selling the artworks, Woodland has kept the first painting she made with her original three rats. articles.title: High voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel threatens Netanyahu
articles.summary: A historic turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel positions Arab parties as kingmakers against the far right.
articles.body:
Palestinian citizens of Israel have turned out in unprecedented numbers for Israel’s parliamentary elections, with some towns reporting participation rates exceeding 70 percent.

Historically, however, Arab towns have witnessed lower participation rates in Israeli elections, ranging between 45 and 65 percent in recent years.

This electoral surge from Palestinian citizens of Israel now threatens to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing coalition.

For many from this contingent, who might normally have abstained from voting, this election was perceived as a chance to defeat a government that was totally hostile to Palestinians and Arabs at large.

There have been a number of measures enacted by Israel’s current right-wing government that encouraged high turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel in this election. These include attempts by Jewish settlers to establish an outpost on Palestinian land in Majd al-Krum in the Upper Galilee.

“The people who were indifferent to the elections, and who did not want to participate or vote, the matter provoked them,” Hussein Manna, a resident of Majd al-Krum, told Al Jazeera. “They know very well what awaits us if this government returns to power.”

Netanyahu and his far-right allies, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, have heavily targeted Arabs in their campaigning. But this appears to have backfired and instead encouraged Palestinian citizens of Israel to go out and vote for Arab parties, the Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am).

Preliminary reports suggest that these parties could secure up to 17 seats combined , enough to prevent Netanyahu from reaching the required 61-seat majority.

“It is fateful for Netanyahu and for his political future, and it is also fateful for the State of Israel because it will determine its identity later on,” Walid al-Omari, Al Jazeera’s bureau chief in Palestine, said.

He added that if Netanyahu’s coalition remains in power, Israel “will move more towards racism and towards extremism”.

Ahmad Tibi, head of the Arab Movement for Renewal, told Al Jazeera: “The first goal: bringing down the government of Netanyahu, Smotrich, and Ben-Gvir, the government of crimes, the government of failure, and the government of racism and incitement against us.”

But he warned that the leaders of almost all parties opposed to Netanyahu have ruled out an alliance with the Arab parties.

“What is the excuse? It is post-October 7, and this is a racist position,” Tibi stated. “We are ready to extend our hands to cooperate with the opposition to bring down the speaker of the Knesset [Amir Ohana] and also to prevent Netanyahu from becoming the head of a transitional government.”

In exchange for this tacit support, the Arab parties have strict demands. “The next alternative government is not our knight in shining armour and will not be a government of peace, but it will not have Ben-Gvir and Smotrich and the racist ministers,” Tibi said.

“Accordingly, we will make room for the establishment of another less bad alternative government that dialogues with us on issues that concern our society as a safety net for our society, such as issues of crime, violence, personal security, home demolitions and racism, as well as an important political horizon on our part because we have a clear political position on the occupation and on the crimes of the occupation and war crimes.”

Al-Omari said if Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party, Netanyahu’s main opponent in the election, gets 53 seats, and Ra’am, headed by Mansour Abbas and most acceptable to the Eisenkot-led alliance, wins eight, then a coalition of 61 members could be formed.

When the prospect of high Palestinian voter turnout emerged, Netanyahu and the far right launched a frantic campaign, warning supporters about this.

Netanyahu posted AI-generated images of Arab voters to incite his base, a move the Joint List condemned as an attempt to create a “misleading scene”.

Mohannad Mustafa, an academic and expert in Israeli affairs, believes that Netanyahu considers the Arab vote illegitimate. He said racist fearmongering and a hostile environment during the campaigning set a dangerous precedent.

“This is also what led to the assassination of Rabin in 1995 when Netanyahu said Rabin’s government in approving the Oslo Accords relies on the Arab lists in the Knesset,” Mustafa added, referring to former Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

There were also reports of right-wing parties deploying activists to polling stations, which was widely interpreted as a form of intimidation against Palestinian citizens of Israel who were voting.

“I toured the ballot boxes here in Taibe, Tira and Qalansawe; in every box there is [someone] obstructing the electoral process and slowing it down specifically so that long queues form at the boxes,” Tibi stated.

He believes the right hoped such tactics would make Palestinian citizens of Israel tired of waiting in line at the polls and leave without voting. Instead, he saw the community’s “determination to stay until the voting is done”.

The outcome of the election carries significance for the broader Middle East, with Netanyahu launching the genocide in Gaza, killing more than 74,500 Palestinians, and assaults on Syria, Lebanon and Iran during his term.

Tariq Hamoud, a political analyst, noted that an Israeli government without Netanyahu might have implications for these ongoing military engagements.

What could determine the election, though, is that Netanyahu “bears responsibility for the security failure on October 7, which opened the doors” to these wars.

articles.title: What to expect at Worcester's Bridges of Light festival
articles.summary: Organisers promise an "immersive" experience as they prepare for the event's second showing.
articles.body:
Organisers have promised a high quality and "immersive" experience as a light festival returns for its second year.

Bridges of Light in Worcester, set to begin on Wednesday and continue into Thursday, will feature a number of illuminated displays across the city centre.

It follows what was described as a "really successful" event in 2025 and project lead Elaine Knight, from organiser Severn Arts, said she could not wait to see people's reactions.

"It makes you really proud, it makes you really emotional and it makes you feel like the last 12 months of hard work… was really worthwhile," she told the BBC.

"It's why we do it, we're all really passionate about the arts and culture in Worcester as a city. It's really important for us that we give those opportunities for people to see work like this."

The event will be held each day from 18:00 to 21:00 GMT and is billed as having Worcester's "imagination and creativity" at its heart.

Knight said the artworks incorporated the experiences of residents, adding: "It's about local people having their stories told and having their voices heard."

She said it was important for Severn Arts to have the opportunity to provide a "high quality experience" on people's doorstep.

As well as being able to stand back and watch the displays, Knight said many of them would be interactive.

"It's really great for us to have that really immersive experience where the audience can change it for themselves and the rest of the people watching," she added.

Among the displays will be Seven Echoes, which will feature illuminations on Worcester Bridge, and an accompanying choral soundscape recorded with more than 50 volunteer singers.

There will also be a food court on Copenhagen Street, where traders will be serving refreshments from 17:00 GMT on both days.

articles.title: Sam Fender's Newcastle pre-sale moved after 'bot attack'
articles.summary: Fender says a "sophisticated bot attack" affected a website selling tickets for his Newcastle shows.
articles.body:
Sam Fender has rescheduled the pre-sale for his tour's homecoming show after a "sophisticated bot attack" reportedly affected a ticketing website.

In a post on Instagram, the 32-year-old said he had been told the site Gigantic had been hit for his shows at St James' Park in Newcastle in summer 2027, prompting him to move the sale back 24 hours to 09:30 GMT on Thursday.

It came days after he removed a ticket category from sale due to his unhappiness with the costs for fans, which he said were out of his control.

Gigantic, which is advertising general sale tickets on Friday, has been approached for comment.

Fender announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour last week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester.

The musician from North Shields did not give details for any other venues being affected by the "bot attack", but a source told the BBC they did not have any issues buying tickets for the London show.

Fender wrote: "Being told that there's been a sophisticated bot attack to the Gigantic ticket site which is impacting the St James' Park pre-sale.

"We're going to have to move the Newcastle pre-sale to 09:30 tomorrow to ensure real fans get the tickets."
